title: Juan Benet Neuropodcast
summary: Conversations with the people building the frontier of neurotechnology and brain science.
bottleneck: Neurotechnology spans many technical approaches; shared conversations help make the frontier legible.
work: Juan Benet talks with researchers and founders about brain-computer interfaces, neural data, connectomics and the future of intelligence.
evidence: The published episodes below document the conversations. Reach, adoption and downstream effects are separate questions.
plRole: Juan Benet hosts the conversations, published through PL Neuro.

resources.title: Adam Marblestone — We Are Massively Underinvesting in the Human Brain
Allison Duettmann — Why We Don't Have to Die: Cryonics, Uploading, and Existential Hope
Konrad Kording — The Power of a Single Neuron and Simulating the Brain
Tom Oxley — BCI Without Opening the Skull, the Race With China, and the 2040s
Jacques Carolan — The Mission to Get Breakthrough Brain Treatments to Everyone
Ben Rapoport — Treating Paralysis and Digitizing Neural Data
Max Hodak — Restoring Sight, Growing Neurons on Silicon, and Expanding Human Intelligence

sourceNote: All seven podcast episodes listed on PL Neuro at 29 September 2026 are included. This is a published collection; current production and future release cadence are not established by the public listing.

title: BCI Roadmap Series
summary: A shared roadmap for taking brain-computer interfaces from scientific promise to practical use.
bottleneck: Clinical revenue, consumer adoption, public understanding and capital formation each present different barriers.
work: Publish a strategic overview and focused roadmaps on the barriers to BCI adoption.
evidence: Read the published overview and Roadmaps 1–3 below. Publication is evidence of a shared roadmap, not proof that the barriers have been resolved.
plRole: Protocol Labs publishes the BCI Roadmap Series through PL Neuro.

PL BCI Roadmap Series: Roadmap 2 — Expanding Neurotechnology to Consumer Products
PL BCI Roadmap Series: Roadmap 3 — Popularizing the Promise of Neurotechnology

sourceNote: The overview and Roadmaps 1–3 are published. Roadmap 4 — Increasing Venture Capital Flows — is listed as coming soon; it is not presented as a published edition.

title: IERR 2025 · Impact Evaluator Research Retreat
summary: An immersive research retreat on impact evaluation and public-goods funding mechanisms.
bottleneck: Research on impact evaluation and distributed funding needs sustained exchange across approaches and disciplines.
work: The retreat focused on the Impact Evaluator framework, evaluation mechanisms and distributed funding systems, bringing together researchers and practitioners.
evidence: The public retreat record marks the event as concluded. Its existence does not by itself establish causal impact or a return on funding.
plRole: The retreat was organised by a coalition of researchers and practitioners. This entry does not attribute sole delivery or impact to Protocol Labs.

title: d/acc Residency · Edge City Patagonia
summary: A four-week residency to prototype defensive-acceleration ideas in a real community setting.
bottleneck: Cross-field ideas need a place to become prototypes and be tested in context.
work: The residency was designed for residents to prototype projects across AI, robotics, governance, self-sovereign tools, cybersecurity, resource allocation and information integrity inside Edge City’s popup village.
evidence: The public residency record marks the programme as concluded. Programme completion and demonstrated downstream impact are different claims.
plRole: Protocol Labs hosted the residency within Edge City Patagonia.
